channel.title: Explainer tags on AI Security Atlas
channel.description: Recent content in Explainer tags on AI Security Atlas

item.title: Access Control
item.description: Authentication, scoped tokens, authorization-aware retrieval and least privilege that limit who can reach what.

item.title: Action Approval
item.description: Typed channels, bound approvals and gated executors that keep an agent’s consequential actions under control.

item.title: Adversarial Perturbation
item.description: Gradient-guided pixel noise or token suffixes that push a model toward an attacker-chosen output.

item.title: Behavior Gate
item.description: Release gates that rerun held-out probes and refuse a model or adapter that misbehaves.

item.title: Benchmark Data
item.description: Ground-truth evaluation sets, answer keys and baseline traffic used to measure whether an attack or defense really works.

item.title: Classifier / Judge
item.description: A detector, filter model or LLM judge whose verdict decides what passes or how something is scored.

item.title: Data Audit
item.description: Defenses that scan, deduplicate, cluster or quarantine training data before and after training.

item.title: Downstream Sink
item.description: Tools, runners, peer agents and interpreters that act on model output and so turn text into consequences.

item.title: Evaluation Rigor
item.description: Fresh splits, reference checks and honest success counting so a reported number means what it claims.

item.title: Exposed Attack Surface
item.description: Endpoints, tool arguments and defaults that are open or unchecked unless someone locks them down.

item.title: Extraction Probe
item.description: Attacker queries and measurements that steal a model or infer private facts such as membership, hidden size or another tenant’s prompt.

item.title: Guardrail Bypass
item.description: Ways to slip harmful input past a detector, filter or text-only control without tripping it.

item.title: Indirect Injection
item.description: Hidden instructions planted in pages, emails, images, tool descriptions or tool output that an agent later reads and obeys.

item.title: Inference Server
item.description: The serving runtime, with its slots, prompt and KV caches and shared state across requests.

item.title: Input Filter
item.description: Classifiers, normalization, perplexity checks and screens that inspect input before the model acts on it.

item.title: Leak Path
item.description: The route that carries a secret, a memorized record or another tenant’s data out to someone who should not see it.

item.title: LLM Agent
item.description: An assistant or group of agents that holds credentials, memory and tools on a user’s behalf.

item.title: Measurement
item.description: Scores, accuracies, timings and verdicts used to tell whether an attack succeeded.

item.title: Minimal API Output
item.description: Returning labels instead of scores, rounding and truncating so an API gives away less to extraction.

item.title: Model File
item.description: The serialized checkpoint, adapter or tensor bytes that sit on disk before a loader turns them into a running model.

item.title: Model Internals
item.description: Activations, attention heads, embeddings, logits, scores and control tokens inside a forward pass.

item.title: Model Loader
item.description: The deserializer, template renderer or repo code that runs when a model file is opened.

item.title: Model Weights
item.description: The learned parameters (full weights, adapters, soft prompts, UNets) that decide what a model is.

item.title: Output Filter
item.description: Validation and encoding applied to model output before it is shown or executed.

item.title: Poisoned Data
item.description: Attacker-planted, triggered or leaked training rows that change what a model learns.

item.title: Prompt Hardening
item.description: Instruction hierarchy, delimiting, spotlighting and system-prompt rules that tell a model to treat content as data.

item.title: Prompt Injection
item.description: Instructions an attacker types straight into the prompt to override the operator’s intent or extract what should stay hidden.

item.title: Provenance & Pinning
item.description: Defenses that pin hashes, sign manifests and trace lineage so a swapped or edited artifact is refused.

item.title: Resource Abuse
item.description: Inputs or settings an attacker chooses to drive up compute, tokens or server load.

item.title: Resource Limits
item.description: Token caps, step budgets, rate limits and cost monitoring that bound how much work one request can trigger.

item.title: Retrieval Pipeline
item.description: The embedder, vector index and ranked context that a RAG system puts in front of the model.

item.title: Retrieval Poisoning
item.description: Planted or unauthorized documents that get into a retrieval index and so into the model’s context.

item.title: Robust Training
item.description: Adversarial training, DP-SGD and regularization that make a model harder to fool or to mine for data.

item.title: Safe Loading
item.description: Allowlist loaders, data-only formats and sandboxed parsing that stop a model file from running code.

item.title: Server-Side Policy
item.description: Fixing decoding settings, templates, stop rules and allowed input types on the server instead of trusting the client.

item.title: Tampered Artifact
item.description: A swapped adapter, edited tensor, injected pickle opcode, rewritten template or altered code that gets in through the model supply chain.

item.title: Tenant Isolation
item.description: Per-tenant cache salts, session binding and partitioning that keep one customer’s state away from another’s.

item.title: Training Data
item.description: The clean demonstrations, labels, preference pairs and corpora a model is trained or fine-tuned on.

item.title: Training Pipeline
item.description: The training, fine-tuning, reward-model or preference-optimization process that turns data into weights.

item.title: Trusted Documents
item.description: Knowledge bases, emails, tool results, task data and other content an application or agent reads as legitimate context.

item.title: Victim Tenant
item.description: The user or tenant whose data, prefix or session ends up exposed to another party on shared infrastructure.
